newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria president appeals for IMF funding.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria president appeals for IMF funding.

text.p: Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov on Monday appealed to the International Monetary Fund for help to stabilise the economy before the planned introduction of a currency board.

In a letter to International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Michel Camdessus, Stoyanov said the interim government expected to be appointed this week could start preparation of an economic programme with the IMF and World Bank which would include urgent structural reforms.

"The interim government together with the central bank is prepared to receive senior IMF officials to begin immediate negotiations for the introduction of a currency board," said the letter made available to Reuters.
"At the same time we would like to consult with the IMF mission...for financial stabilisation in the transition period before the introduction of a currency board."
The IMF proposed the implementation of a strict monetary mechanism last year to halt the freefall of the national currency, the lev, and to restore confidence in ailing banks.
The system requires levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing financial powers of the government and the central bank.
"As the latest events show, we made significant progress in the peaceful solution of political problems in leading Bulgaria to the right path for overcoming the deep economic crisis," Stoyanov said.
Opponents of Bulgaria's Socialist government held nationwide strikes and 30 days of mass demonstrations to force elections 20 months early.
The IMF and the European Union had said no help would be forthcoming until the political crisis was sorted out.

"Beside the technical aid from the IMF, it is vital to find other extraordinary forms of urgent financial help," said Stoyanov in the letter. "Without it it will difficult to overcome the grave economic crisis."
Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said at the weekend Bulgaria would need external funding in order to implement a currency board.

With inflation estimates of 43.8 percent for January 1 to 25 alone, hyper-inflation has become a factor for the first time. Long queues of consumers have formed outside bread shops to stockpile food before prices go up the next day.
The lev fell to 3,100 per dollar on Monday from 600 in the beginning of the year and the central bank has exhausted its arsenal of monetary instruments to support the lev.
